title: Data tables
hint: Upload a business dimension table (UTF-8 CSV or Excel) to show the IDs in analysis results as business names; field names must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, digits and underscores — pick the join key column in “Configure bound properties”.

confirm.clearContent: The table structure and bindings are kept; results fall back to the raw values.
confirm.deleteContent: Bound properties become invalid and the data cannot be recovered.

upload.allColumnsEmpty: Every column of the file is empty; check that the header and the data are in the same worksheet
upload.tableTooLarge: The table content exceeds the 10MB limit (Excel compresses well, so the original file may be small) — split it and upload again
upload.payloadTooLarge: The file content exceeds the server limit (10MB) — split it and upload again
upload.fileTooLarge: The file exceeds the 30MB limit — split it and upload again
upload.noWorksheet: The Excel file has no worksheet
upload.emptyWorksheet: The first Excel worksheet is empty
upload.dragText: Drag a CSV / Excel file here, or click to upload

help.popoverTitle: What a data table is and how to use it
help.whatIsLead: maps an “ID → business name + business attributes”, turning codes like
help.whatIsTail: in analysis results into business names such as “Epic Longsword”.
help.problemOnlyId: Results only contain IDs, which tell you nothing → show the business name instead
help.problemGroupLead: Group by “quality / resource / item category” when the events do not carry those properties → the dimension table supplies them at
help.problemGroupMid: , so no tracking change is needed — and
help.problemSharedRule: Several cards share one business definition: change the dimension table once and the related queries follow
help.usageUploadLead: Upload a table: CSV or Excel (the first worksheet is used), optionally with metadata rows
help.usageBind: Configure bound properties: pick the join key column + the properties to bind (multiple allowed); fields with the same name can be bound in one click
help.usageShowTerm: unmatched values fall back to raw values
help.usageShowTail: , while drill-down, linkage and export still use the raw values
help.ruleLimits: One table ≤ 10MB / 200,000 rows / 100 columns; field names must start with a lowercase letter, contain only lowercase letters, digits and underscores, and be ≤ 50 characters
help.ruleKeyTerm: you pick the join key column
help.ruleKeyDesc: (not fixed to the first column): its values are matched against the values of the target property
help.ruleUpdate: Update data: incremental (overwrite by key, rows that no longer appear are kept) / replace (whole table); versions switch atomically and the old data is kept if the switch fails
help.ruleDelete: Deleting a table also invalidates its bound properties; a table with the same name can be created again
help.ruleCache: After changing a table or its bindings, query results refresh once the cache expires (about 1 minute)
help.ruleScope: Value mapping currently covers event analysis; funnel and retention follow

wizard.uploadDone: Parsed successfully ({{fileName}}) — you can upload again
wizard.uploadHint: UTF-8 CSV or Excel (.xlsx/.xls, the first worksheet is used); the first column is the primary key
wizard.droppedColumns: Ignored {{count}} all-empty columns (no values in the data rows): {{columns}}; the first column is used as the primary key
wizard.markerDetected: Data table metadata rows detected: {{items}}; the marker column has been stripped — choose in the next step whether to use it
wizard.labelRow: Row 2 looks like field descriptions (Chinese names); it is used as display names and not imported as data. If it is not a description row, merge it into the header and upload again
wizard.renamedHeader: The header “{{from}}” is not a valid field name and was changed to {{to}}; you can rename it to a meaningful English name in step 2
wizard.invalidField: Invalid field name: {{name}} (must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, digits and underscores, ≤ 50 characters)
wizard.duplicateField: Duplicate field names found — fix them before continuing
wizard.adoptNames: Use ##name as the field display names
wizard.adoptTypes: Use ##type as the field data types
wizard.declaredFirst: Trust the types declared in the file (otherwise they are inferred from the data; conflicting rows are listed one by one before import)
wizard.dupKeys: ; {{count}} duplicate primary keys in the file (the last row wins)

update.title: Update data table: {{name}}
update.modeIncr: Incremental (insert or update by primary key; old rows that no longer appear are kept)
update.dragHint: The header and column order must match the current schema; UTF-8 CSV or Excel (the first worksheet) is supported
update.previewSummary: Parsed {{success}} rows and dropped {{dropped}} rows; the table currently holds {{current}} rows
update.dupKeys: {{count}} duplicate primary keys in the file (the last row wins);
update.atomicNote: the active version switches atomically after submit; if the submit fails, the live data stays unchanged.
update.labelRowSkipped: Row 2 looks like field descriptions (Chinese names); it was skipped and not imported as data
update.failed: Update failed (the original data is kept)

binding.title: Configure bound properties (data table: {{name}})
binding.alertText: The join key column {{key}} of data table {{table}} has type “{{type}}”, so it can only be bound to properties of type {{targets}}; every other field is derived into a “property@field” dimension property. Properties with an incompatible type are greyed out in the dropdown with the reason shown.
binding.purgeConfirm: Delete this invalid bound property permanently? (this cannot be undone)
binding.unbindConfirm: Unbind this bound property? (it becomes invalid first and can then be deleted permanently)
binding.labelTitleTip: In query results this property is shown by the business name in the dimension table column “{{column}}” (in blue); hover to see the raw value
binding.noLabelTip: The dimension table has no usable business name column (only ID-like columns), so this property is not mapped and the raw value is shown instead
binding.noMapping: Not mapped (no usable business name column)
binding.autoNoFields: No fields can be bound automatically; the name columns {{columns}} need no mapping (their values are already business names)
binding.autoNoMatch: No properties share a name with the data table fields, so nothing can be bound automatically (pick properties manually)
binding.autoDone: Bound {{count}} same-named fields in one click: {{fields}}
binding.needProp: Select at least one property to bind
binding.searchProp: Search by property key or display name; select several to bind them at once
binding.useCustom: Bind using “{{key}}” as the property key
binding.keyColumnTip: Property values are matched against this column
binding.labelFieldTip: Query results show this column instead of the property ID; when no column is picked, the name column is used by default{{current}}. The “property@field” columns below are derived dimensions, not display columns.
binding.emptyHint: Click “+ Add property” to create a bound property

table.keyInvalid: A data table name must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, digits and underscores, up to 50 characters
table.nameExists: A data table with this name already exists in the project
table.busy: This data table is being updated; please try again later
table.noFields: The data table has no fields and cannot be updated
table.rowLimitExceeded: A table holds at most {{limit}} rows; this update would produce {{rows}} rows. Split or trim the data.

binding.propBound: This property is already bound to the data table
binding.noFields: The data table has no fields; properties cannot be bound
binding.keyColumnNotFound: Join key column {{column}} is not a field of the data table; available: {{options}}
binding.propNotFound: Event attribute {{prop}} does not exist (this project has not collected it; the binding would always match 0 rows)
binding.typeMismatch: Type mismatch: data table key column {{column}} ({{keyType}}) and event attribute {{prop}} (declared type {{declared}}) are not in the same family; the binding would always match 0 rows
binding.eventTimeGranularityRequired: Binding an event time requires selecting a time granularity
binding.granularityNotAllowed: A time granularity is only needed when binding an event time

import.primaryKeyTypeMismatch: Primary key is not a valid {{type}} value or is too long
import.fieldTypeMismatch: Field {{field}} is not a valid {{type}} value or is too long
